points: Ours is the only dataset in the table that stores the timed action behind each motion (a program with an onset and a duration) and interventions during the motion.
States are stored at 120 Hz, against 12 to 60 Hz in the datasets that report a rate, and a scene holds a median of 24 and up to 113 objects, against at most 15 in the others.

With 506k simulations it is second in size to CoPhy (572k), whose sequences hold 2 to 6 objects. Its 13k scenes are each simulated under up to six actions and their counterfactual edits; PhysInOne has more scenes (154k) and more families (71).
Counterfactual runs are also in CoPhy, DynSuperCLEVR and NewtPhys. The 490k question-answer pairs are the most in the table.

What ours does not have: deformable bodies and fluids (Physion, NewtPhys and PhysInOne do), and stored image channels. Depth, optical flow and scene flow are rendered from the stored states on demand.
caption: Table 6 of the appendix. Objects: median (maximum) where measured, otherwise as published. ✓ present, ✗ absent, ✓† derivable from the stored states on demand, – not reported. A timed action is a program with an onset and a duration, given as an input. An intervention is a change during the motion, not only at the start. Our scenes are sampled worlds, each simulated under up to six actions and their counterfactual edits. NewtPhys and DynSuperCLEVR also re-simulate counterfactuals, on 53 scenes and 1.2k videos. Bold: best; underlined: second. References for each dataset are in the appendix.
appendix_sentence: Against the datasets of Table 6, our scenes are larger and our states are stored at a higher rate than in any that reports these numbers.
